body.en: *Matter* exists as solid, liquid or gas. By composition it is either a mixture or a pure substance. A homogeneous mixture (air, sugar solution) has uniform composition throughout; a heterogeneous mixture (sand in water) does not. Pure substances are elements (one kind of atom, e.g. Cu, O$_2$) or compounds (atoms of different elements in a fixed ratio, e.g. H$_2$O, CO$_2$).
body.kn: ದ್ರವ್ಯವು ಘನ, ದ್ರವ ಅಥವಾ ಅನಿಲ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಯ ಆಧಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅದು ಮಿಶ್ರಣ ಅಥವಾ ಶುದ್ಧ ವಸ್ತು. ಶುದ್ಧ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಧಾತುಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು.

heading.en: Matter, SI Units and Significant Figures

tagline.en: How chemists classify matter, the seven SI base units, temperature scales, scientific notation, significant figures, precision versus accuracy and dimensional analysis.

myth.en: Zeros never count as significant figures, so 2.500 g and 2.5 g are the same measurement.

truth.en: Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant: 2.500 g (4 s.f.) was measured to the nearest milligram, 2.5 g (2 s.f.) only to the nearest tenth of a gram. Leading zeros only locate the decimal point, so they do not count. Trailing zeros after a decimal point were actually read off the instrument, so dropping them throws away information.

say.en: Matter: pure substances (elements, compounds) and mixtures (homogeneous, heterogeneous).
Seven SI base units: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd. T(K) = t(°C) + 273.15.
Significant figures: leading zeros never count; trailing zeros count after a decimal point; exact numbers have infinitely many.
× and ÷: fewest significant figures; + and −: fewest decimal places.
Precision = agreement among readings; accuracy = agreement with the true value.

goal.en: How chemists classify matter, the seven SI base units, temperature scales, scientific notation, significant figures, precision versus accuracy and dimensional analysis.

task.en: How many significant figures does each number have?

explain.en: Count from the first non-zero digit. Zeros between digits always count; trailing zeros count when a decimal point is shown; in scientific notation count only the digits of N.

takeaway.en: Matter: pure substances (elements, compounds) and mixtures (homogeneous, heterogeneous).

narration.en: Many people think: Zeros never count as significant figures, so 2.500 g and 2.5 g are the same measurement. Actually: Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant: 2.500 g (4 s.f.) was measured to the nearest milligram, 2.5 g (2 s.f.) only to the nearest tenth of a gram. Leading zeros only locate the decimal point, so they do not count. Trailing zeros after a decimal point were actually read off the instrument, so dropping them throws away information.

problem.en: Convert 25 °C to kelvin and to degrees Fahrenheit.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Convert 25 °C to kelvin and to degrees Fahrenheit.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Convert 25 degrees Celsius to kelvin and to degrees Fahrenheit.
K equals 25 plus 273.15 equals 298.15 kelvin.
degrees Fahrenheit equals (9 over 5)25 plus 32 equals 45 plus 32 equals 77 degrees Fahrenheit.
So the answer is 298.15 kelvin; 77 degrees Fahrenheit.

problem.en: A block of aluminium has a mass of 5.4 g and a volume of 2.0 cm³. Find its density.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A block of aluminium has a mass of 5.4 g and a volume of 2.0 cm³. Find its density.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A block of aluminium has a mass of 5.4 grams and a volume of 2.0 cubic centimetres. Find its density.
Density equals mass divided by volume.
d equals 5.4 grams divided by 2.0 cubic centimetres equals 2.7 grams cm to the power minus 3.
So the answer is 2.7 grams cm to the power minus 3.

homework.en: Convert −40 °C to kelvin and to °F. What do you notice?
A 10.0 cm³ piece of copper has a mass of 89.6 g. Find its density.

narration.en: Recap. Matter has mass and occupies space; it may be a solid, liquid or gas. Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous; pure substances are elements or compounds. SI has seven base units, including the kilogram, kelvin and mole. K = °C + 273.15 and density = mass / volume.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ದ್ರವ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ರಾಶಿ ಇದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದು ಜಾಗ ಆಕ್ರಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದು ಘನ, ದ್ರವ ಅಥವಾ ಅನಿಲವಾಗಿರಬಹುದು. ಮಿಶ್ರಣಗಳು ಏಕರೂಪ ಅಥವಾ ಭಿನ್ನರೂಪ; ಶುದ್ಧ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಧಾತುಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು. SI ಪದ್ಧತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಿಲೋಗ್ರಾಂ, ಕೆಲ್ವಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೋಲ್ ಸೇರಿ ಏಳು ಮೂಲ ಏಕಮಾನಗಳಿವೆ. K = °C + 273.15 ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ = ರಾಶಿ ÷ ಗಾತ್ರ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Matter has mass and occupies space; it may be a solid, liquid or gas.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ದ್ರವ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ರಾಶಿ ಇದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದು ಜಾಗ ಆಕ್ರಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದು ಘನ, ದ್ರವ ಅಥವಾ ಅನಿಲವಾಗಿರಬಹುದು.

say.en: Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous; pure substances are elements or compounds.
say.kn: ಮಿಶ್ರಣಗಳು ಏಕರೂಪ ಅಥವಾ ಭಿನ್ನರೂಪ; ಶುದ್ಧ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಧಾತುಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು.

say.en: SI has seven base units, including the kilogram, kelvin and mole.
say.kn: SI ಪದ್ಧತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಿಲೋಗ್ರಾಂ, ಕೆಲ್ವಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೋಲ್ ಸೇರಿ ಏಳು ಮೂಲ ಏಕಮಾನಗಳಿವೆ.

say.en: K equals degrees Celsius plus 273.15 and density equals mass divided by volume.
say.kn: K equals degrees Celsius plus 273.15 ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ = ರಾಶಿ divided by ಗಾತ್ರ.
